name: Hotel Workers — Back of House

stations.why: The banquet floor the series shares with the kitchen: hot boxes, chafers and the room set that has to be right before the doors open.
The room itself, turned under the state's own hotel ergonomics rule: the cart staged outside, the belt panic device proven, and the bed walked around rather than reached across.
The plant behind every room on the floor: dosing lines checked against the SDS, the washer loaded to the scale, and the ironer's guard proven before a hand ever gets near the rollers.
The other end of the banquet floor from the hot line: tables lifted two-handed, chairs stacked to the limit, and the risers locked before the stage is loaded.
The stockroom before the first room: the new product looked up on its SDS, every bottle filled at the dispenser and labelled, the cart loaded heavy-low to its plate, and nothing ever mixed.
The banquet floor against the clock: rounds rolled onto the truck, stage decks lifted by a called team, cables ramped and the exits walked, with the doors held rather than a corner cut.

The laundry's most dangerous machine on a bad day: a wrapped sheet cleared under the operator's own lock at the disconnect and the steam valve, the heat waited out, and the guards back before the restart.

summary: The hotel jobs that carry the injuries: turning a room with a housekeeping cart under the state's own hotel ergonomics rule and a panic button on the belt, the laundry plant's chemicals and folder, and a banquet changeover lifted right.
union: UNITE HERE hotel housekeepers, laundry and banquet staff
